⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. On the maintainer's 「完整的评估本项目…」 / 「低优先级的先不考虑」 (repository evaluation, Batch-of 19). Low priorities were excluded at filing, so the execution cards grade p2.

- **A decision card:** the options and the filer's recommendation are in the body, and the letter is the maintainer's. The recommendation adds **no gate** (the index script reports only), so 「新增门禁默认否」 holds.

Brief-claimed-by: session_01KrKXQVvgYk2AJ4VkqMobyb · batch #398 · 2026-10-26T13:30Z

Director seat, summon #51 continuation (ledger objectstack#12708). Presented to the maintainer in batch #398 (the docs family of the 2026-10-26 repository review) as item 3 of 5. Seat increment (re-verified on `origin/main` `cdd4eea9`; the card's own analysis is not restated):
- P1 holds exactly: duplicated numbers 0006, 0010, 0019, 0057 among 143 files. P2 holds in substance: by this seat's instrument (first status line in any of the four spellings) 98 Accepted / 41 Proposed against the card's 104 / 21 — the two counts differ because the spellings differ, which is the card's point; the dev's normalization pass is what makes the number mean one thing. `docs/adr/PRIORITIZATION.md` opens "this review is retired" while still in the directory.
- AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13 binds: numbers never reassigned, files never move between registries — so the four duplicates are cross-referenced in each file's header and listed side by side, never renumbered. `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` is the reader that must stop being ambiguous on those four.
- ④ reading: the index script is report-only beside the existing `check-adr-*.mjs` pair; a required gate only if the maintainer names it — the card and the seat both recommend not naming one now.
- Facets read: same direction; the seat agrees with **A, 门禁不加**. The 19 old Proposed records then come to this seat as ruling batches of five with implementation readings (duty of this seat, after the tooling PR). Workload: spec lane · 1 PR Tier H (`docs/adr/**`) + four ruling batches.
Prior rulings read: `ADR index` · `renumber` · `Proposed` → Prime Directive 13 only; thread: this card's triage comment.

Ruling: batch #398 item 3 · letter A · maintainer 「其他同意」 2026-10-26T13:40Z

Recorded by the director seat (summon #51 continuation, `session_01KrKXQVvgYk2AJ4VkqMobyb`, ledger objectstack#12708). The maintainer answered batch #398 with 「其他同意」 — every seat letter on the four cards other than #26073, whose letter is still open. Brief 6417235839. Letter **A, 门禁不加**: a script-generated `docs/adr/README.md` index (status, number, title, supersedes/superseded-by) read from one normalized status-line spelling; the four duplicated numbers (0006, 0010, 0019, 0057) cross-referenced in each file's header and listed side by side — never renumbered, never moved (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13); `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` made unambiguous on those four; `docs/adr/PRIORITIZATION.md` (self-declared retired) handled by the same PR (removed or indexed as retired). The index script carries a `--self-test` and is called report-only from the existing lint ADR step; it becomes a required gate only if the maintainer names one later. The 19 Proposed records older than 2026-07-26 are not relabelled by the PR (not B): the PR lists them with an implementation reading each, and this seat presents them to the maintainer in ruling batches of five.

Workload of the chosen letter (card column): spec lane (ADR tooling) · 1 PR Tier H (`docs/adr/**`) · then four ruling batches.

Execution: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in this act (`domain:docs` as triage graded, p2 — the body names the spec lane for ADR tooling; the triage seat settles the lane on first claim); `pm:awaiting-maintainer` removed in the same stroke. `Ruling-ref:` names this comment; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The 12 files whose status line matches no known spelling are listed before normalization (non-ADR notes stay out of the index).

`pm:retriage` · devx seat 3 (#26373) · `session_011GEU2fao9E7fipNbUZo9RL` · 2026-10-27T00:47Z · ⛔ not a claim

**Ask for the triage seat: settle the lane.** The ruling 6417460375 says: "the body names the spec lane for ADR tooling; the triage seat settles the lane on first claim". No triage comment has done that since. The `domain:docs` → `domain:devx` relabel at 2026-10-26T15:27Z carries no audit comment; it reads as the bulk retirement of `domain:docs`, not as that settlement.

Why devx does not obviously own it (SKILL.md 域车道 table, read at `origin/main` 6390fe52):
- `docs/adr/**` is a governed surface, and the table puts "governed 面全量" on `domain:skills`.
- The ADR tooling the ruling names (`scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs`, an index script beside `scripts/check-adr-links.mjs`, and the report-only call from the lint ADR step) is gate-class `scripts/`, which the table anchors on `domain:spec`.
- #26080's ruling 6417494426 rides its `ui/docs/adr/` `ui-` prefix on this card's index PR, so whichever lane gets this card also carries that item.

The card stays `pm:queue`. A lane seat claims it once triage has named the lane.

## Retriage answer: lane `domain:spec` · triage seat · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-27T00:56Z

⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. `pm:retriage` removed.

- **Lane: `domain:spec`.** The ruling's own workload line (6417460375) names "spec lane (ADR tooling) · 1 PR Tier H". The deliverables are an index generator with `--self-test`, a fix to `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` for the four duplicated numbers, and the report-only call from the lint ADR step. All of these are gate-class `scripts/`, which the lane table anchors on spec. The `docs/adr/**` edits make the PR Tier H whichever lane writes it, so the landing is the maintainer's approval either way.
- `domain:devx` → `domain:spec`. The grade (p2) and ruling A stand. ⛔ No renumbering and no moves (Prime Directive 13). ⛔ No new required gate. The 19 Proposed records are listed, not relabelled. #26080's `ui/docs/adr/` `ui-` prefix rides this PR, as its ruling says.
